text:
Who to Contact, and When

Save the relevant links and local numbers before you need them. Their hours and services change, and some only work in one country.

During or soon after a psychedelic experience

Fireside Project: U.S.-only according to its current FAQ; phone or text psychedelic peer support at 623-473-7433, daily from 11 a.m. to 11 p.m. Pacific Time.
TripSit live chat: browser-based harm-reduction chat for people using drugs and the people supporting them.

Global crisis and emotional-support directories

Find A Helpline: a global directory of free helplines, many offering phone, text, online chat, or WhatsApp. It is not psychedelic-specific, but it can put a human on the other end quickly.

U.S. crisis chat and text

988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline: U.S. call, text, and chat for suicidal or mental-health crises.
Crisis Text Line: U.S. text, chat, and WhatsApp support, with partner text lines listed for Canada, the UK, and Ireland.

Integration and post-experience support

ICEERS Support Center: up to five free online integration sessions for challenging experiences.
CPEP online peer group: a free confidential monthly group for post-psychedelic difficulties.
Cheetah House: resources, consultations, and support groups for meditation-related difficulties, including chat-based peer support.

questions.Q1: PASS: each paragraph opens on its point: the first priority, the room fixes with their reason, what the reminder is for, then the anchor part's point
questions.Q2: PASS: every act is the helper's own, with its purpose: the dangers removed, the lights dimmed and the extra people out because they're overwhelmed, the reminder because a trip can make them lose track; one calm person as the lead, a second as backup when it's more than one can hold
questions.Q3: PASS: which things exactly: keys, stove, roads, balconies, pools, weapons, the phone; the lights, the extra people; place, date and time, the substance; who leads and who backs up, and when
questions.Q4: PASS: no terms a reader would not know; "anchor" is the heading's word, said in the sentence as the calm person who leads
questions.Q5: PASS: each turn has what it turns on: since a trip makes them lose track; the opposite of alone is too many people; backup when one person cannot hold it
questions.Q6: PASS: dangers, room, what to say, then who should be with them
questions.Q7: PASS: every fact is about the person in front of them now
questions.Q8: PASS: the anchor part is one point, under its heading
questions.Q9: PASS: nothing compressed: the reminder's facts one a sentence, as said aloud; the anchor part one step a sentence

question_text.Q1: Why am I reading this sentence, and do I know it before I have to work through it? (the point first, in each sentence and each paragraph; a study after the question it answers; a term explained where it is first used, never in a sentence after it)
question_text.Q2: What is each instruction for, said in the reader's terms, and is it something the helper does ("have someone go with them"), not a rule stated as a fact ("someone goes with them")?
question_text.Q3: Which thing exactly? (pools of water, not water; any substance, not anything)
question_text.Q4: What does each word act on, or mean here? (adjunct remedy; known-genuine) Is every term a high-school graduate wouldn't know (enterocytes, BPC-157) explained once, where it is first used, and common ones (a vitamin) left alone? Is each mechanism explained by what it does in the reader's experience (dopamine "for motivation (by showing us what is important to pay attention to)"; DeltaFosB "preventing that learning from really clicking"), not by where it sits or what it looks like ("a chemical blanket", "the slower one underneath")? (E375)
question_text.Q5: Why does each sentence follow from the one before? (every but, so, because and this has what it turns on)
question_text.Q6: Is this the order the reader is thinking in, and does each idea sit next to what it continues?
question_text.Q7: Does each fact help this reader now, in their case (the same kind of thing they face, not just the same topic)?
question_text.Q8: Does each item belong in the group it is put in?
question_text.Q9: Is anything compressed? (one step a sentence, the small words that carry the relation, no space before mg)
